title: Slovak parliament votes to end postal voting from abroad
seoTitle: Slovakia’s overseas voting bill: what changes for voters abroad
dek: Lawmakers approved a bill that would replace postal ballots for citizens abroad with in-person voting at Slovak diplomatic missions. The bill still requires the president’s signature.
happened: Slovakia’s parliament passed the election bill by 79 votes to 71 on November 24. Under the bill, Slovaks abroad would cast ballots in person at diplomatic missions, including embassies and consulates, instead of sending their ballots by post.

sides.says: Prime Minister Robert Fico said the change was intended to prevent fraud. AP reported that he offered no evidence to support that claim. The bill’s sponsors said voting at diplomatic missions preserves the right to vote from abroad.

Opposition lawmakers say the change would make voting harder for Slovaks abroad. They urged the president to withhold his signature and said they would challenge the measure in the Constitutional Court.

next: President Peter Pellegrini said he was likely to sign the bill if his legal advisers raised no major objections. TASR reports that the change is due to take effect on January 1, 2027, if enacted.
summary: Slovak lawmakers voted to replace postal voting from abroad with in-person voting at diplomatic missions. The president’s decision and a promised court challenge are the next steps.
